intake.matter_summary: Represent buyer/developer in the purchase of 4400 Kestrel Point on Lake Verdant; central issue is whether access over a neighbor's gravel lane is a recorded easement or a revocable license. Negotiate and paper a purchase agreement that secures permanent access.

conflicts_check.notes: No current or former representation of the seller Renard, the neighbor Delahaye, or the City. Delahaye is an adverse but unrepresented adjoining owner; no conflict. Cleared by both partners.

time_entries.narrative: Initial client interview with Talbot Meskin; intake of goals, four-cabin plan, and access concerns; open matter.
Review 1978 recorded access instrument, 1971 plat, and title commitment; note absence of legal description and Schedule B access exception.
Legal research on easement appurtenant versus revocable license and location of an indefinitely described right of way under Meridian law.
Client counseling call re: access risk, title exception, and options to cure; discuss strategy.
Prepare strategic settlement and negotiation plan (SSNP); map interests, BATNA, confidential facts, and access-cure options.
Draft purchase-agreement access contingency and cure/title-objection provisions.
Negotiation session with seller's counsel re: access characterization, contingency deadline, and price; follow-up notes.
Revise purchase agreement; refine access-cure and closing-condition language after negotiation.
Inquiry into City of Brightwater proposed vacation of Verdant Shore Road; counsel client on structuring a road-vacation contingency.
Coordinate with surveyor Brummond re: fixing easement centerline/width; correspondence to seller's counsel.
Final negotiation and review of purchase-agreement terms; client memo on recommended deal.
